_comment: Arena layout for the 2026 NASA International Lunabotics Championship.
Single source of truth, read by BOTH ends: arena_server on the robot and
arena_minimap on the base station. That is the point of the file - the base
station draws the arena from its own local copy instead of having the robot
stream a map or mesh over the link. Only the robot pose crosses the network,
which is one small message rather than a costmap.
Coordinates are in the ARENA frame: the guidebook Origin Point, at the centre
of the front (south) wall, +X east, +Y north, Z up at grade.
PROVISIONAL. Guidebook 3.1 calls the layout images placeholders from the prior
two-team configuration, and 5.7 says the same of the fiducial rail. The prose
also disagrees with Figure 2 on arena size - '~10 m long and ~10 m wide'
against a dimensioned 9.14 x 8.10 m bed. Re-measure into this one file.
If both ends do not read the SAME file, the base station will draw an arena
the robot is not navigating in, and nothing will report an error.

bed._comment: Regolith bed extent, used by the minimap to size its view.

zones.name: starting_zone
zones._comment: 2.25 m square against the front wall, offset west of the Origin Point. That asymmetry is what tells you which way you are facing on first acquisition.

zones.name: excavation_zone
zones._comment: Overlaps the starting zone: 5.4.6 allows excavating from anywhere within it, including the starting zone.

zones.name: obstacle_zone
zones._comment: The only zone where contact costs points: 30 per rock touched or crater crossed, up to 90 (6.2.4, 6.2.5). Rocks may be moved and craters filled in the excavation zone, never here.

zones.name: target_berm_area
zones._comment: The scoring target. Only berm volume inside this box counts (5.2.2). Figure 2's legend and its scaled drawing both give 2.2 x 0.9 m while the 5.2 text says 1.5 x 0.9 m; the drawing is used here because it is dimensioned.

fiducials._comment: Team-supplied ArUco markers on the arena's 80/20 rail, mirroring perseus_simulation's lunabotics_fiducials. marker_length_m is the printed SQUARE, not the plate: 0.238 m on a 0.35 m plate, the rest being quiet zone. It must match vision/aruco_detector's marker_length or the two disagree about scale by 1.47x.
